goal: choose active layer and move selection onto layer
positive_oracle: Select current layer Metals, assign object A, panel and model both reflect same LayerId
negative_oracle: Assign onto locked/unavailable layer must refuse explicitly

behaviour_reference.source: OM9_Milestones/M01 - CAD Shell, Viewport/L2-03-14 - Febe Matrix Layers Objectinfo Superselect/reference/text/m8book1__p54-57__the-layers-menu.md
behaviour_reference.quote: It also organizes things by turning off or hiding those parts you don't need to see right at the moment; selecting things you need to use all at once, and "locking" layers you don't wish to change with a certain operation.
behaviour_reference.decision: The manual says locking protects a layer from certain operations. Moving objects onto a locked layer is such an operation, so it is refused, explicitly and without a transaction.

method: The behavioural source is the extracted Matrix9 manual section shipped with the milestone; QymCAD is consulted only for panel technique.

observed_symbols: gui.rs:354 comment: THE ONE DOORWAY OF THE FEATURE TREE
planned_anchors.what_is_missing: One doorway for a user action: the idea OM9 keeps. QymCAD has no layer and therefore no lock rule for it.

implemented_api_before_this_task: session/layers.rs: set_current_layer (creates the missing preset group and makes the preset current), assign_layer (creates missing presets then assigns), set_layer_property (visible/locked), layer_id(slot), select_layer(slot)
layer_command.rs: LayerChoice { None, Slot, Existing } and parse() with ambiguous-label refusal
ui/layers.rs: the palette paints the current row through layer_id(slot) == document.current_layer
gap_found_by_this_task: assign_layer never read the target layer's lock: moving geometry ONTO a locked layer succeeded, which is exactly the operation the manual says locking prevents (negative oracle). The fixture L1 caught it (RED: 1 passed; 2 failed).

Fixed in the controller: the lock is checked after the target is resolved and BEFORE any LayerAction is applied, so the refusal costs no transaction and leaves the selection where it was (Error::Permission("layer is locked")).

Pinned, unchanged because they already held: create+current in one batch; assignment does not steal the current layer; an empty selection is a no-op; the panel reads the same LayerId the document holds.
reuse_decision: ADAPT the single doorway of gui.rs; ADD the lock rule for assignment in the controller.
